title: Trump on NBC 'Meet the Press': Won't Unfreeze Iranian Assets; Will Help Iran Destroy Its 440kg Uranium Stockpile if Deal Reached — Day 99 of US-Iran War
detail: On June 7, 2026 (Day 504 / Iran War Day 99), President Trump sat for a wide-ranging interview with NBC 'Meet the Press' anchor Kristen Welker that aired Sunday morning, setting out his clearest public framework yet for ending the US-Iran conflict. On sanctions: Trump said he would NOT unfreeze Iranian assets or offer early sanctions relief as part of any peace deal — 'If they behave, if they do a good job, we start talking.' On the nuclear stockpile: Trump said the US will help Iran retrieve and destroy its estimated 440.9 kilograms of highly enriched uranium (enriched to 60%) if a deal is reached — reversing earlier statements about 'entombing' it — framing US technical assistance as a confidence-building measure. Trump insisted Iran hadn't accepted a deal because 'they're strong and proud,' not because talks had fundamentally broken down, and expressed optimism. On the diplomatic front, Iran's top supreme leader adviser told CNN that talks were 'at a deadlock' and 'the ball is in Trump's court.' Iran accused the US of ceasefire violations after American forces shot down six Iranian drones near the Strait of Hormuz over the prior 48 hours and struck Iranian coastal radar stations on Goruk Island and Qeshm Island. Back-channel communications via intermediaries continued. Oil prices edged toward ~$88/bbl on deal-optimism, while 10-year Treasury yields held near 4.47%. Trump's June 7 Sunday show appearance ahead of the G7 Évian summit (June 15–17) signaled he is using media appearances to pressure Iran directly.

media.caption: Trump on NBC 'Meet the Press' sets out Iran deal conditions: no early asset unfreeze, will help destroy 440kg uranium stockpile — Day 99 of US-Iran war

title: Senate-Passed $70 Billion ICE/CBP Reconciliation Funding Bill Awaits House Vote — Week of June 8
detail: On June 7, 2026, the $70 billion immigration enforcement reconciliation package — which the Senate passed 52-47 on June 5 after an 18-hour 'vote-a-rama' — was awaiting a House floor vote tentatively scheduled for the week of June 8. The bill funds ICE and Customs and Border Protection operations for three years through the end of Trump's second term, covering detention capacity, deportation flights, technology infrastructure, and border wall construction. An amendment stripping the controversial 'anti-weaponization' fund (which would have allowed political investigations of opponents) was defeated in the Senate, remaining in the final text. Senate Republicans were unanimous except Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), who voted against it. All Democrats voted against the bill except Sen. Michael Bennet (D-CO), who was absent. House Republican leadership canceled Friday votes June 6 due to attendance concerns ahead of the upcoming recess window, making the week of June 8 the final realistic window for passage before Congress breaks. Failure to pass the House would force Senate Republicans to restart the reconciliation process from scratch. The bill is considered a top Trump second-term legislative priority alongside the already-signed 'One Big Beautiful Bill.'

media.caption: Senate-passed $70B ICE/CBP reconciliation funding bill awaits House floor vote the week of June 8, 2026

title: Trump Confirms G7 Évian Attendance (June 15–17) — Iran Deal Diplomacy and AI Agenda Set
detail: By June 7, 2026, the White House had confirmed that President Trump would attend the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France (June 15–17), with Trump stating he plans to depart Washington after hosting a UFC fight at the White House on June 14. French President Macron, who is hosting the summit, secured Trump's attendance by offering a post-summit dinner at Versailles — a significant diplomatic gesture aimed at managing Trump's frustration with European allies over their refusal to join the US-Iran military campaign. The G7 agenda includes artificial intelligence governance, cross-border crime and drug trafficking, and trade policy. Iran deal diplomacy is expected to dominate the margins: UK Prime Minister Starmer, German Chancellor Merz, and Canadian PM Mark Carney are all expected to press Trump to accept a written framework deal with Iran that would end the oil supply disruption. French officials said Macron has been in direct contact with Iranian intermediaries and believes a G7 announcement on Iran could be possible if Trump moves on sanctions flexibility. Trump's attendance at Évian is his first G7 since returning to office and represents a significant shift from earlier 2025 reports that he might skip the summit entirely.

media.caption: Trump confirms G7 attendance at Évian-les-Bains June 15–17; Iran deal diplomacy and AI governance on agenda
